summary: Generation 5 recovery confirmed that the remaining five-worker live contention canary is blocked by batch fan-in, not by PIN exclusivity. race5 v3 is fresh and correctly routed as a timing-only PORTFOLIO_BARRIER_ENTER, but it appears only once in the 24-candidate unified shard array. WAVE-20260917-MESH-03 disperses workers across that array; no v3 entrants existed at 00:47Z. The current regression proves barrier transformation but not that required_contenders distinct workers are concurrently routable. No entrants, RELEASE, winner, collisions, or PASS evidence were synthesized; production /w remains unpromoted.

spawn_candidates.title: Fix batched contention-barrier fan-in
spawn_candidates.reason: Unified hash sharding spreads workers away from a single barrier candidate, so required_contenders=5 is not concurrently routable despite the barrier route itself being structurally correct.
acceptance: An explicit open barrier with required_contenders=5 and BATCH EXPECTED 10 admits exactly five distinct workers through durable timing-only coordination, with the remainder immediately reallocating.
The five admitted workers share one valid no-authority RELEASE and race one fixed G000001 PIN, producing exactly one owner claim and four genuine collision receipts.
No PIN attempt occurs before RELEASE and no late PIN occurs after timeout.
Ordinary candidates preserve current deterministic unified sharding and pay no barrier coordination cost.
Regression test covers the full batched routing path, not only single-candidate barrier transformation.
